label: update gate high when observed evidence favours S2 / last chose a2 (GO, D1)
terms: (phase == GO) * np.tanh(belief_lo) ;; (phase == D1) * np.tanh(belief_lo) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_action, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == D1) * table(prev_action, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_state, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == D1) * table(prev_state, {1: -1, 2: 1}) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1)
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 40. Timing: ~1.0 (saturated) at D2 with no meaningful variation, ~0.52 at GO, ~0.25 at D1 falling late in the episode; timing alone R^2 0.59. Beyond timing the magnitude is an a1-vs-a2 axis at GO (largest, ~+/-0.4) and D1 (~+/-0.15): high when the ideal-observer belief says S2 is good (graded tanh(belief_lo), weight -0.28 at GO, -0.12 at D1) and when the previous choice was a2 (+0.13 GO, +0.09 D1); small extra effects of last reached state (S2 raises at GO, lowers at D1) and a lower value after a rewarded previous trial. Not driven by future reward or time since reversal. Observed-only terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.78 (dev 0.80) vs all-observed table reference 0.90 and all ceiling 0.96; the model policy decile alone reaches 0.93, so dropping the model own choice logit costs ~0.15, i.e. the unit tracks the agent upcoming a2 tendency more tightly than the ideal-observer belief plus last trial can.

issues: The scores reproduce. On test the 8 terms give R^2 beyond timing 0.7807 (total 0.911, timing alone 0.593), and the fitted weights match the stated ones (GO tanh(belief_lo) -0.284, D1 -0.119, prev_action a2 +0.129 / +0.092, prev_state S2 +0.036 at GO / -0.068 at D1, prev_reward +1 -0.066 / -0.026).

The direction claims hold in the profile residuals. GO residual by belief decile runs from +0.41 (S2 favoured) to -0.47 (S1 favoured). At D1 it runs from +0.25 to -0.17. D2 residuals are about 0.005 or smaller, consistent with saturation. Trials since reversal (0.01) and this trial's reward (0.00) add nothing, as claimed.

The comparison to 'all observed 0.90' is misleading. That reference includes 'this choice x state', which at D1 and GO is the UPCOMING choice, a future variable. Upcoming action alone, (phase==GO)*table(action) + (phase==D1)*table(action), scores 0.797 on test. So the truly observed ceiling is nearer the belief decile (0.73) plus last trial (0.66) combination, and the terms are close to it. The 'about 81% of the ceiling' framing understates how close the terms are to what observed variables allow.

A residual systematic error remains at GO after switch-type or ambiguous trials. Misses show under-prediction at GO after a1 S2 r (+0.152), a2 S2 u (+0.128) and a1 S1 u (+0.084), and over-prediction at D1 after a1 S1 u (-0.118). Adding last_is indicators for those patterns only raises test R^2 to 0.791. The gap looks like the agent's upcoming switch decision, which observed variables do not capture.

None of my attempts beat the original by much. Removing prev_state and prev_reward gives 0.752. A signed model-based last-trial evidence term gives 0.773. A full last-trial lookup table plus belief gives 0.776. Adding belief x cover and the choice two trials back gives 0.778. Summed recent-choice history gives 0.772. Belief x prev_action gives 0.776. Two-slope belief gives 0.766. So the 8 terms are near-optimal for observed-only additive shapes.
The prev_state and prev_reward effects are small (weights 0.03-0.07). The explanation calls them small, so this is not an overclaim.
